title: Strengthening AI Regulatory Frameworks: The EU-LAC Digital Alliance Statement
executive_summary: On November 16, 2023, during the AI Alliance Assembly in Madrid, EU and Latin American and Caribbean (LAC) countries reaffirmed their commitment to a Digital Alliance aimed at enhancing cooperation on digital policy and regulatory frameworks for artificial intelligence (AI). Following a joint declaration in July 2023, participating nations, including Argentina, Colombia, and Mexico, proposed initiatives to promote convergence in AI regulation, emphasizing the need for best practice exchanges and the establishment of regulatory sandboxes. The upcoming EU Regulation on AI will set safety and rights-based requirements for AI providers. The alliance aims to foster innovation while ensuring human rights are respected, with a focus on linguistic inclusivity and ethical guidelines. Regular dialogues will facilitate the sharing of experiences and support for startups in developing trustworthy AI solutions.
characteristics: The EU and LAC countries have established a Digital Alliance to enhance human-centric digital cooperation and regulatory convergence on AI.
A forthcoming EU Regulation on AI will set safety and rights-based requirements for AI system providers, including regulatory sandboxes for innovation.
The initiative emphasizes the exchange of best practices and operational guidelines for AI regulation among participating states.
It aims to foster AI development across linguistic diversities, ensuring inclusivity in technology.
Regular dialogues will be maintained to align digital policies while promoting innovation and protecting human rights.
practical_applications: Establishment of the Digital Alliance EU-LAC, a framework for cooperation among EU and Latin American and Caribbean countries to promote human-centric digital cooperation and convergence of digital policy and regulatory frameworks on AI.

Implementation of the upcoming Regulation on AI in the EU, which includes requirements for AI system providers based on risk assessments and the creation of regulatory sandboxes for testing innovative AI systems.
Commitment by participating states to exchange best practices and operational regulatory measures on AI, including governance mechanisms for monitoring AI regulation.
Development of a bi-regional investment package for the implementation of the Digital Alliance, tailored to local contexts and needs.
Regular dialogues among states to share information and foster the development of AI regulations that promote innovation, human capital, and infrastructure while respecting human rights.
